# Network construction and analysis

## Identity resolution

Person resolution precedes graph construction. Each merged identity should be
auditable through stable identifiers, affiliations, publications, or an
explicit manual decision. Diacritics, name order, initials, and name changes
must be handled without erasing uncertainty.

## Network layers

The analysis begins with at least two graphs:

1. a publication co-authorship graph;
2. an MSc co-supervision graph, where researchers are linked when they jointly
   supervise the same thesis.

An author–thesis or supervisor–thesis bipartite representation should be kept
as the source of any projected person-to-person graph.

## Validation and sensitivity

Reported rankings should be checked against alternative time windows,
reasonable population definitions, edge weighting choices, and treatment of
disconnected components. Genuine Erdős paths receive an additional manual
evidence check.

This chapter will grow with executable analysis as the data model settles.
